hook_text: No branches. No app. Tens of billions of rands a year. Meet the stokvel.
clip_script: The stokvel turns neighbours into a bank: everyone contributes monthly, each takes a turn to receive the pool — school fees get paid, stock gets bought, funerals get covered. Tens of billions of rands move this way every year, among people banks overlooked. This is Indigenous Knowledge Systems — knowledge grown over generations, and it is not folklore; it is working infrastructure made of trust. And the law must guard it: when the San people's hoodia knowledge was patented for profit without consent — the crime called biopiracy — it took years to win recognition and a share. Knowledge is property too, and the street owns some.
visual_style: A circle of hands passing a growing pot of coins around a kitchen table, cutting to a courtroom gavel and a rooibos field at golden hour.
mood: Proud, warm, then quietly fierce on the biopiracy turn.
pacing: Steady heartbeat rhythm for the circle, a hard cut for the patent theft, resolving on the win.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson: development, the six signs, and the knowledge your community already owns.
